outlier.evidence: Ratings 4, 4, 3, 4, all at confidence 4. Reviewer_Jqx8's 3 is one point below the rest and rests on the same missing-DynamicFusion objection. All four answered the rebuttal and kept their scores.

checkable_claims.claim: With ground-truth depth and masks as input, the reconstructions still fail to reproduce the input view (Fig. 5: motorbike, truck, airplane, man on the floor, helicopter).
checkable_claims.evidence: In Fig. 5 the predicted motorbike, truck and airplane are coarse or incomplete, although the paper presents them as successes; the man on the floor and the helicopter are the paper's own failure cases (lines 358-361). The authors conceded that nothing makes the output match the input depth; adding that constraint raised IoU from 32.5 to 35.1.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper neglects DynamicFusion and the RGB-D non-rigid fusion line of work.
checkable_claims.evidence: References [1]-[53] contain no RGB-D non-rigid fusion method, while lines 3-5 call the setting 'more realistic yet more challenging' than prior work. The camera-ready adds a 'Fusion-based 4D reconstruction' paragraph (DynamicFusion, VolumeDeform, KillingFusion, SurfelWarp).

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not discuss any non-deep-learning method at all.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 77-78 cite classical NR-SfM (Bregler et al. 2000 [3], Zhu et al. 2014 [51]) and line 82 cites variational RGB-D scene flow [16], one sentence each. The narrower point, that no fusion method is discussed, is correct.

checkable_claims.claim: Line 347 reports the oracle with the ground-truth flow-field, which should give near-perfect results.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 347-349 say 72.6 IoU was obtained 'when using the ground-truth flow-field', but lines 341-342 say the predicted flow was applied to ground-truth meshes. The rebuttal confirmed the second reading, so the text is wrong. Reviewer_tafs in B flagged the same contradiction.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not discuss its limitations.
checkable_claims.evidence: There is no limitations section. Checklist 1(b) points to Sections 4.4-4.5, which show three failure cases (lines 358-361) and the oracle gap but never discuss the ground-truth inputs or the supervision.

checkable_claims.claim: The title 'from Monocular Videos' is misleading for a method that needs RGB-D input.
checkable_claims.evidence: Submitted title 'Class-agnostic 4D Reconstruction from Monocular Videos'; abstract line 2 says 'unconstrained monocular videos'; lines 96-97 require RGB-D frames, instance masks and camera matrices. The camera-ready title drops 'Monocular'.

checkable_claims.claim: All experiments are on synthetic data.
checkable_claims.evidence: Only SAIL-VOS 3D, extracted from GTA-V (lines 282-286).

checkable_claims.claim: Line 79 overclaims that the method 'doesn't rely on any templates or priors', although it learns a prior from data.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 79 makes the claim; the shape prior is learned from SAIL-VOS 3D meshes. The rebuttal narrowed 'priors' to 2D keypoints.

checkable_claims.claim: Flow inference is independent of shape inference, not a joint solution.
checkable_claims.evidence: Eqs. 3-5: the velocity field sees only the static feature z_p, never the shape; shape depends on flow, not the reverse. Training is joint (Eq. 6, line 228), which is all the rebuttal addressed.

checkable_claims.claim: Baseline inputs are not stated; PIFuHD uses no depth at inference while FREDO does.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4.2 (lines 291-298) never states the baselines' inputs. The rebuttal confirms PIFuHD and OFlow got RGB only at test time, while FREDO got ground-truth depth. Under the camera-ready's revised protocol, with retrained baselines, the SAIL-VOS 3D margin over OFlow is 5.9 mIoU, against 12.3 in the submission.

checkable_claims.claim: Training needs ground-truth 3D correspondences (scene flow).
checkable_claims.evidence: L_temp (Eq. 8, lines 253-255) uses ground-truth vertex correspondences.

checkable_claims.claim: Results cover 5 categories and never test unseen ones, so 'class-agnostic' is unsupported.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 285-286 list person, car, truck, motorcycle and airplane; no class is held out. The camera-ready adds a zero-shot test on dog, gorilla and puma.

checkable_claims.claim: Results for non-human categories are of low quality (helicopter, truck).
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1 IoU: person 50.5, truck 23.5, airplane 20.4. The Fig. 5 vehicles are coarse.

checkable_claims.claim: Neural Deformation Graphs uses the SMPL human model, so it says nothing about class-agnostic methods (discussion, 2021-08-23).
checkable_claims.evidence: A claim about another paper, not this one. The authors replied that NDG uses no SMPL model and needs four calibrated depth cameras; Jqx8 did not answer.

rebuttal.evidence: No review was edited after posting. All four replied and kept their scores: Reviewer_7c6w on 2021-08-19 ('persist in the current rating'), Reviewer_Jqx8 on 2021-08-23 ('lean to maintain my current rating'), Reviewer_nToe on 2021-09-01 ('Maintaining original rating after rebuttal'), Reviewer_SY53 on 2021-09-02 ('would vote for rejection').
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: 7c6w accepted that DynamicFusion has no public code but dismissed the 3DPW results as humans only: 'If the paper had show results on generic objects (not just humans) in real videos ... I would have been been more supportive.' Jqx8 named SurfelWarp and KillingFusion as runnable; the authors posted qualitative SurfelWarp results on 2021-08-31, 09-01 and 09-03. No A reviewer and not the AC mentioned them, although nToe and SY53 replied after the first posting. SY53 rejected the depth-consistency fix (+2.6 IoU) as a patch, not the sanity check it meant, and called the solution 'half-baked'. nToe adopted the others' DynamicFusion concern and kept its quality and novelty objections.

ac.evidence: The meta-review cites 'four negative reviews from expert reviewers' and names the shared concern: no discussion or comparison with methods 'along the line of DynamicFusion'. It accepts that DynamicFusion has no released code, but says the many follow-ups make 'a thorough comparison' crucial. It does not mention the SurfelWarp results posted in the discussion, nor quality, supervision or novelty.

main_reasons_for_decision: No discussion or comparison with DynamicFusion and its follow-ups (all four reviewers and the AC); the submission cites none of them
Low reconstruction quality despite ground-truth depth and masks, worst on non-human classes (SY53, Jqx8, 7c6w, nToe)
Ground-truth inputs at test time and 3D supervision in training, with synthetic-only evidence; the rebuttal's 3DPW test covers humans only (nToe, SY53, 7c6w)
Novelty judged a combination of OFlow and PIFu (nToe, 7c6w)
Unanimous 3-4 ratings at confidence 4, kept after the rebuttal

outlier.evidence: Ratings 7, 8, 7, 6. Reviewer_Gayd's 8 is one point above two 7s; without it the mean is 6.67, still an accept. Its review is uncritical (see inattentive_reviews).

inattentive_reviews.evidence: An 8 ('Fantastic work!') that says 'I was satisfied with the discussion of related work', although the submission cites no RGB-D non-rigid fusion method. It never mentions the ground-truth depth, masks and cameras at test time, or that the baselines got RGB only, and it calls the results 'strong'. It did not reply to the rebuttal.

Three hours, confidence 3, 'Math/other details were not carefully checked', two vague concerns. Its post-rebuttal update says 'the experiments with only a synthetic dataset are limited', ignoring the 3DPW real-data results in the general response. It raised 5 to 6 anyway and never posted in the discussion.

checkable_claims.claim: DynamicFusion and Neural Deformation Graphs, class-agnostic RGB-D methods with a canonical space, are not discussed or compared.
checkable_claims.evidence: Neither appears in references [1]-[53].

checkable_claims.claim: The PIFuHD comparison is unfair (RGB against RGB-D), and it is unclear how OFlow was adapted.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4.2 is silent on baseline inputs; the rebuttal confirms both baselines got RGB only at test time.

checkable_claims.claim: Line 35: per-frame segmentation is not enough; masks must be tracked across frames.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 34-36 present off-the-shelf segmentation as sufficient, but the method needs masks m_ij that follow object j through all frames (lines 106-107).

checkable_claims.claim: The oracle paragraph (lines 338-350) contradicts itself about which of mesh and flow is ground truth.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 341-342 apply the predicted flow to ground-truth meshes; lines 347-349 report the result 'when using the ground-truth flow-field'.

checkable_claims.claim: Z_far is set at a fixed distance from Z_near, whatever the object's size.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 130-132; the distance is not given in the main text.

checkable_claims.claim: All experiments use ground-truth inputs on one synthetic dataset.
The discussion of related work is satisfactory.
checkable_claims.evidence: No RGB-D non-rigid fusion method is cited. Four reviewers across both committees flagged this, and the camera-ready adds a paragraph on it.

checkable_claims.claim: The authors include failure cases.
checkable_claims.evidence: Fig. 5 bottom right and lines 358-361.

checkable_claims.claim: FREDO beats the baselines by a large margin, though they were designed for slightly different tasks.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1: 32.5 against 20.2 mean IoU for OFlow. Only FREDO received ground-truth depth. Under the camera-ready's revised protocol, with retrained baselines, the margin is 5.9 mIoU, and ONet beats REDO on DeformingThings4D++.

rebuttal.evidence: FhQ8 posted 'raising my rating to 7' on 2021-08-31 and edited its review that day. Lqt3 edited on 2021-09-13: 'I update my final score from 5 to 6'. Reviewer_tafs edited on 2021-09-10 to say 'I'm keeping my original score' (7). Reviewer_Gayd neither replied nor edited.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: FhQ8 had asked for qualitative real-data results and a comparison with a fusion method. The 3DPW visualisations and the SurfelWarp comparison convinced it: 'The comparison with SurfelWarp clearly shows that the data-driven FREDO is able to track larger deformation.' It stayed surprised that video depth estimation worked on moving people. Lqt3 found the scene-flow answer fair but still called the synthetic-only evaluation limited. tafs got answers on window size, positional encoding, run time and the oracle, and kept 7.

ac.evidence: The meta-review counts three initially positive reviewers and one borderline negative, and says the positive ones 'became more positive' with real-world results; only FhQ8 rose among them. It says the negative reviewer 'did not interact', but Lqt3 raised 5 to 6 on 2021-09-13. It never mentions the missing fusion literature, the ground-truth inputs or the baselines' inputs, and calls the paper 'a positive step' on 'the very difficult problem'.

main_reasons_for_decision: A hard, little-explored task; the paper is a credible first step (Gayd, tafs, AC)
Large margins over learned baselines in Table 1 (tafs, Gayd)
Rebuttal results on real 3DPW videos and the SurfelWarp comparison (FhQ8, AC)
Clear writing and a sound design (Gayd, tafs, Lqt3)
All four final ratings at 6 or above

issues_only_a: Output does not reproduce the observed input view despite ground-truth depth; the method may be 'partially broken' (SY53)
Low absolute quality on non-human classes, which undercuts 'class-agnostic' (SY53, Jqx8, 7c6w)
Misleading 'Monocular' title and overclaims at lines 3 and 79 (Jqx8, SY53)
No comparison with dynamic NeRF methods such as Nerfies and NSFF (7c6w)
Classical registration and fusion (ICP with a deformation grid, TSDF fusion) not tried in place of the learned flow and aggregation (SY53)
Flow inference decoupled from shape; missing NR-SfM reference Dai et al. 2012 (Jqx8)
issues_only_b: Fixed Z_far offset whatever the object size (tafs)
Effect of window size N and positional encoding; inference time (tafs)
How much occlusion the method handles; results by occlusion level (FhQ8)
Why image features are needed when depth is given (FhQ8)
Per-frame segmentation versus masks tracked across frames (FhQ8)
Overlap with multi-frame scene-flow estimation; no comparison with shape-prior NR-SfM methods (Lqt3)
Dependence on the choice of canonical frame (Lqt3)
shared_issues: No discussion or comparison with DynamicFusion-style RGB-D fusion (A: SY53, Jqx8, 7c6w, nToe after the rebuttal, AC; B: FhQ8 only)
Ground-truth depth, masks and cameras at test time; ground-truth meshes and correspondences in training (A: nToe, SY53, 7c6w; B: tafs, FhQ8)
Evaluation on one synthetic dataset only (A: Jqx8, SY53, 7c6w; B: tafs, Lqt3, FhQ8)
Baselines given RGB only while FREDO gets depth, and the setup not stated (A: nToe, 7c6w; B: FhQ8)
Novelty as a combination of OFlow and pixel-aligned features (A: nToe, 7c6w; B: Gayd in passing, Lqt3)
Self-contradictory oracle experiment at lines 338-350 (A: SY53; B: tafs)
verdict: Both committees found the same weaknesses, and the submission confirms each one. FREDO needs ground-truth depth, masks and cameras at test time and ground-truth 3D correspondences in training. It is tested on one synthetic dataset, its baselines got RGB only, and it cites no RGB-D non-rigid fusion work. The split comes from who reviewed and how they weighed these facts. Three A reviewers raised DynamicFusion unprompted, all four sat at confidence 4, and they judged absolute quality; their checkable claims hold (the 'Monocular' title, coarse vehicles in Fig. 5, no unseen-category test). B judged the method against learned baselines and valued a first step on a hard task. Reviewer_Gayd's 8 calls the related work satisfactory and never engaged again; two B reviewers worked at confidence 3. Both forums received nearly the same rebuttal: 3DPW results on humans and a qualitative SurfelWarp comparison. It moved Reviewer_FhQ8, the one B reviewer who had raised the fusion gap, to 7. It moved nobody in A: Reviewer_7c6w dismissed 3DPW as humans only, and no A reviewer or the AC mentioned SurfelWarp. Each AC followed its reviewers. A's objections were accurate for the paper as submitted, though its decisive one was about positioning: in the camera-ready SurfelWarp scores 1.03 mIoU. The camera-ready adds what A asked for, and under its revised protocol the margin over OFlow is 5.9 mIoU, not 12.3.
